verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: copy and run script_path, check its encoding against the theorem, run a vacuity guard with the hypotheses negated
verifiers.reason:
I re-ran the audit and its central claim holds up, so I do not refute it.

RE-RUN. The copy is md5-identical to the audit's script (096208fa…). It exits 0 with all 7 sections agreeing, and the numbers match the audit: T_COEFF = 9.505325e43; ratios 6.579736 and pi^2/6 = 1.6449; [4] 0/400 and 0/400 failures, endpoint zero at 1.570797; [5] first zero 0.9906 against a stretch ending at 0.6613; [6] 0/200 failures; [7] B*l = 1.54562e19 and 1.09292e19 T m. My first run's output was overwritten: another verifier in the shared rederive/ folder wrote to the same run.out. I re-ran under a unique filename, and that run is the one I report.

ENCODING. [1] checks the theorem's algebraic core symbolically: v = sin(sqrt m (x-a)) has its zeros a distance pi/sqrt m apart, W' = (m-q)uv, W(a) = -sqrt m u(a) and W(b) = +sqrt m u(b). The last step (integrate W', compare signs) is printed rather than machine-checked. It is a two-line argument and it is correct. The closed-interval conclusion and the equality case also follow correctly: an endpoint zero forces u(a) = u(b) = 0 and q = m a.e., so u is proportional to v. [2] is Raychaudhuri written correctly: theta' + theta^2/(D-2) + sigma^2 + R_kk = 0 with omega = 0 gives U'' = -(R_kk+sigma^2)U/(D-2), and q = 4 pi G T_kk/c^4 in D = 4. The affine-invariance check is weak: it rescales by one hard-coded factor of 7. [7]'s T^ab = diag(u,u,u,-u) is the right stress tensor for a pure field along z. So the checks test the theorem itself, not a toy version, with two caveats:
(a) [4a], the source-solution test, does not discriminate near the threshold. With the stretch shortened to 0.99 pi/sqrt m it still reports 0/200 failures, because a source that is a distance A >= 0.02 before the stretch enters it already partway through its oscillation. The guarantee for every solution rests on [1] and [4b].
(b) The [6] detector looks for det J changing sign. It cannot see the Weyl = 0 equality case, where det J only touches zero at the endpoint (40/40 missed in my guard). The audit draws Weyl from uniform(-30,30), so this case never arises there, and [6] uses Ricci exactly m rather than a varying q >= m.

VACUITY GUARD (verify/rederive/sturm-vacuity.py, seed 670). With the hypotheses negated, the checks do fail:
- [4a] with L = 0.6 and 0.9 times pi/sqrt m: 164/200 and 25/200 with no zero in the stretch.
- [4b] with q = 0.5m: 70/200. With q = m - 3 sin^2 5x: 9/200.
- A solution starting at a zero, with q = 0.98m: no zero in (0, pi/sqrt m].
- [6] with Weyl = 0 and Ricci/2 = m/4, or Weyl 0.5 with Ricci/2 = 0.5m: 40/40 with no conjugate point.
So the passing checks are not vacuous.

GRADE. The theorem stands as seatindex.py:22-24 states it (sufficient, contiguous stretch). The narrowing applies to how the tree uses it, and the evidence supports it. One nuance sharpens drift (i). The [5] counterexample seats AFTER the stretch, in a benign outside region. For constant q (a uniform ball along a chord), m l^2 >= pi^2 is in fact NECESSARY for universal seating, which I checked with q = 0.98m and a solution starting at a zero. So SR2's 'seating needs' is true under the Sturm-universal reading (spec.py:39, specthm S-2) and false only without that qualifier. This is exactly the scoping the audit proposes, and seatindex.py's own measurement (universality breaks below the frontier) corroborates it.

MINOR, AGAINST THE AUDIT'S OWN TEXT.
- [5] prints 'the Lyapunov bound is the necessary one'. That holds only for the scalar equation; seatindex.py:41-49 strikes Lyapunov necessity once shear is present.
- published_hypotheses (S2) states 'Sturm 1836 assumed continuity' without marking it as recalled rather than read.
Neither point moves the grade. The source remains NAMED-NOT-READ, and the grade rests on computation, which a mathematical theorem permits.

audits.name: Fewster-Osterbrink conclusion: an absolute QEI for non-minimal coupling 'can also be adapted' (expected, not done), with a literature search returning none

source.located: C.J. Fewster & L.W. Osterbrink, 'Quantum Energy Inequalities for the Non-Minimally Coupled Scalar Field', arXiv:0708.2450v2 [gr-qc], 23 Oct 2007 (J. Phys. A 41 (2008) 025402). The sentence is in Sec. 6 Conclusion, pp.20-21, last paragraph. Ref. [31] is C.J. Fewster & C.J. Smith, gr-qc/0702056 (2007).
source.via: The full text of 0708.2450v2 came from alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) earlier in this docket and is cached at scratchpad/d67/src/0708.2450.txt (md5 5ef2edeec5aa48e27368f476cb65da2a). Sec. 6 was read in full. At this stage a fresh alphaXiv call returned 'assistant quota exceeded' and arxiv.org returns 403 at the proxy, so the cached full text is what was read. The rederive script string-matches the quotes against it.

audits.published_statement: FO Sec. 6, final paragraph: 'Finally, our general QEI is of the so-called 'difference' type: it constrains the normal ordered energy density rather than the (Hadamard) renormalised version. This restriction has recently been removed for the minimally coupled field in [31] to obtain an 'absolute' QEI; one would expect that this can also be adapted to the non-minimally coupled field.' Here [31] is Fewster-Smith gr-qc/0702056. Context from the same section: the QEI being upgraded is FO's state-dependent QEI 'for couplings in the range (0, 1/4] in general globally hyperbolic spacetimes' (Thm 4.2 states xi in [0,1/4]). State-independent QEIs are excluded for xi > 0 'at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space'.
published_hypotheses: P1: it is an expectation ('one would expect'), not a theorem. 0708.2450 neither derives nor sketches an absolute NMC QEI.

P2: the expected object is the Hadamard-renormalised ('absolute') counterpart of FO's own state-dependent difference QEI, i.e. a state-dependent absolute bound. FO Sec. 3 already excludes a state-independent one for xi > 0 (massless field, 4D Minkowski).
P3: the expected route is to adapt the Fewster-Smith method (gr-qc/0702056). In 2007 that method was new and proved only for the minimally coupled field.
P4 (implicit): the difference QEI being upgraded has scope xi in (0,1/4] (Thm 4.2: [0,1/4]), a globally hyperbolic spacetime, a timelike geodesic and Hadamard states.
hypothesis_drift: No drift on the FO sentence, qeihps.py:89-90. 'can also be adapted' is FO verbatim (string-matched). 'expected' renders 'one would expect'. 'NOT DONE' is accurate: FO say their own QEI is of difference type.
Kept: the owner's own hypothesis that the NOT-FOUND is an alphaXiv search result and not a non-existence proof (qeihps.py:90-92, 511-512). The tree does not flatten the search into 'does not exist'.

Dropped (minor; a precision, not a change of claim): P2 at qeihps.py:511-512. ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC does not say the expected object is a state-dependent absolute bound. specthm.py:2159-2164 (H_M0) supplies this from context ('state-dependent NMC bounds exist ... and an absolute one is NOT-FOUND'). specthm.py:1049-1053 (R6) does not: it says only 'An absolute QEI for NMC is NOT-FOUND'. Read literally, it could mean an absolute state-independent QEI, and the absence of that is FO Sec. 3's theorem (massless, 4D Minkowski), not a search result.
Unstated, named here: at qeihps.py:90-92 and 511-512 the NOT-FOUND has no search date and no coverage statement. A search result is dated by nature. Recorded, not repaired.

Missed source (a gap in the search, not in FO): Fewster-Kontou 1809.05047v2 p.3 says the opposite: 'as shown in Ref. [28] [math-ph/0611058], nonminimally coupled fields obey state dependent QWEIs of both absolute and difference types'. The qeihps search did not record this. The pages of math-ph/0611058 read here (1-2, 6-9, 22, 24-27) show only the FO difference QEI for NMC; Sec. 3.2-4 (Props 4.5 and 4.6) could not be read. The tree also left out a positive source for its NOT-FOUND: Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815, 'To date no absolute QEIs have been derived for the non-minimally coupled scalar field.'

data_at_publication.quantity: The state of the literature on absolute QEIs (Hadamard-renormalised, local and covariant). This is the only input an expectation depends on; no numerical datum enters.
data_at_publication.value_then: 2007: the first curved-spacetime absolute QEI had just been proved, for the minimally coupled massive scalar only (Fewster-Smith gr-qc/0702056). NMC: difference QEI only (FO). State-independent QEI excluded for xi > 0 (FO Sec. 3).
data_at_publication.value_now: 2020, Kontou-Sanders review: 'To date no absolute QEIs have been derived for the non-minimally coupled scalar field. The root cause is that the operator T^split_ab is not of positive type or symmetric.' 2023, FFKP 2309.10848: their NMC QEI is 'a difference QEIs unlike the absolute one that was possible for the minimally coupled field.' 2024, Kontou 2405.05963: the NMC T^split is not of positive type, so the general inequalities 'cannot be used in this case'; only state-dependent bounds exist. Against this, 2018, 1809.05047 p.3 claims absolute plus difference state-dependent QWEIs citing math-ph/0611058; the pages of that paper read here do not show one. Literature after mid-2024 was not searched (alphaXiv quota exhausted).
data_at_publication.source_now: Cached alphaXiv extractions under scratchpad/d67/src, all md5-pinned: 2003.01815v2, 2309.10848, 2405.05963v2, 1809.05047v2, math-ph_0611058v2 (partial). The rederive script string-matches every quoted sentence.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. By the field's own reviews, FO's expectation was still an expectation in 2024. One of those reviews is co-authored by an author of the contrary 2018 sentence. The NOT-FOUND is corroborated, not overturned. The contrary sentence is a contest and is recorded, not treated as a refutation.

rederivation.outcome: All 32 checks pass; output in rederive/0708.2450-conclusion.out. (A) FO's Sec. 6 sentence and ref. [31] match the md5-pinned cached texts, as do the five later-literature sentences the grade rests on, including the contrary one. The tree's 'can also be adapted' is FO verbatim. (B) The later reviews name one obstruction: T^split is not of positive type for NMC. This was machine-checked on the Minkowski NMC energy density. The kernel on one-particle wavefunctions is K(k,k') = [w w' + k.k' + m^2 + 2 xi |k-k'|^2]/(2 sqrt(w w')), from rho = rho_min - xi Lap phi^2 in signature (+,-,-,-). For the massless s-wave 2x2 minor sympy gives det = -xi (k1-k2)^2 (k1 k2 + xi (k1+k2)^2)/(k1 k2). This is negative for every xi > 0 with k1 != k2, and zero at xi = 0; for example xi = 1/6 with (k1,k2) = (1,2) gives det = -7/24. (C) Numerically, on 40 random 3-momenta, the minimum eigenvalue is about -6e-15 at xi = 0 (positive type), -1.81e-2 at xi = 1e-3, -3.05 at xi = 1/6, -4.60 at xi = 1/4, and -1.40 at m = 1, xi = 1/6. So the Fewster-Smith route FO expected to adapt loses its positivity hypothesis for every xi > 0. This supports why no direct adaptation appeared. It does not prove that no absolute NMC QEI exists: FO's difference QEI gets around the same non-positivity by splitting off a Wick-square term, and this check neither proves nor excludes an absolute analogue built that way.

later_literature.ref: E.-A. Kontou & K. Sanders, 'Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory', arXiv:2003.01815v2 (CQG 37 (2020) 193001)
later_literature.what: States: 'To date no absolute QEIs have been derived for the non-minimally coupled scalar field. The root cause is that the operator T^split_ab is not of positive type or symmetric.' It defines 'absolute' as a lower bound that is local and covariant, and shows that rearranging a difference QEI 'only yields an absolute QEI when the lower bound is local and covariant'. That rules out the reference-state shortcut as a way to count FO's expectation as met.

audits.lacked_data:
FO's sentence is an expectation about a method, not a conclusion drawn from data. No measured quantity enters, so M's hypothesis has no datum to act on. What FO lacked in 2007 was the outcome of the attempt: the Fewster-Smith absolute QEI was months old and covered minimal coupling only.

Evidence for the tree: the Kontou-Sanders 2020 review, FFKP 2023 and Kontou 2024 all record that no absolute NMC QEI has been derived, and they name the obstruction (T^split is not of positive type). The rederive script machine-checks that obstruction: the NMC energy-density kernel has a negative 2x2 minor for every xi > 0, so the Fewster-Smith route cannot be carried over as it stands.

Evidence against the tree: Fewster-Kontou 2018 asserts that absolute state-dependent NMC QWEIs were shown in math-ph/0611058. The readable pages of that paper do not show one.

The later information does not change the tree's use. 'Expected, not done' is still an accurate description of FO, and NOT-FOUND is still the state of the literature as far as it could be read here (through mid-2024). It does sharpen the claim: the NOT-FOUND can rest on a published review sentence instead of a search alone, and the contrary 2018 sentence should be recorded beside it.

The full text is saved at verify/refute/math-ph_0611058v2.full.txt (md5 dce3979d0be2086bfef3d1f8e9aba78f). Sec. 3.2, Props 4.4-4.6 and all of App. B, including the p.25 continuation the audit could not read, are now READ.

(2) Prop 4.5 does not apply to the NMC case:
- Its hypothesis is a *state-independent* DQI, with Q^d_M(f,ω) = Q̃^d_M(f,ω)·1 (verbatim: "Let Q d be any state-independent locally covariant difference QI").
- FO's NMC DQI is state-dependent. App. B gives Q_M(f,ω0) = Q̃_M(f,ω0)·1 + φ²_M(S_M(f)), and S_M(f) is nonzero for ξ > 0.
- The paper's other route (Sec. 3.2) is rearrangement, which works iff eq. (10) holds. The paper checks eq. (10) only for the Wick-square DQI (App. A).
- App. B shows only the difference form for 0 ≤ ξ ≤ 1/4 and its nontriviality. It never states or derives an AQI for NMC.
- What the paper does is redefine 'absolute QI' to allow state-dependent bounds (Def. 3.1, pp. 7-8). It does not exhibit one for NMC.

(3) Effect on the contested sentence. Fewster-Kontou 1809.05047 p.3 says NMC fields obey "state dependent QWEIs of both absolute and difference types" as "shown in" math-ph/0611058. The cited paper does not show this explicitly. At most the sentence is an unchecked inference from the broadened definition. It is still recorded as a contest, not quoted as an error, per the fluctuation.py precedent. But it no longer stands as unresolved counter-evidence against the NOT-FOUND.

(4) Later literature does not change the picture. discover_papers was run twice (all dates, and 2023 onward). It found no absolute NMC QEI. The 2026 Modave lectures (2605.18964, Fliss, read at source, pp. 27-29) discuss NMC only through FO's and FFKP's state-dependent bounds, which use normal ordering (:φ²:), and cite no absolute one. This also extends the searched window beyond the audit's mid-2024 limit. It was a search, not an exhaustive census, so the post-2024 caveat should be softened but kept.

(5) The audit's computation is correct. I re-derived the s-wave projection independently: angular averages <k·k'> = 0 and <|k-k'|²> = k1² + k2², with diagonal entries a(1+4ξ)/2. This gives det = -ξ(k1-k2)²(k1k2 + ξ(k1+k2)²)/(k1k2), and -7/24 at ξ = 1/6, (k1,k2) = (1,2). Both match the audit. The rederive script also re-runs ALL PASS. verifiers.reason:
I re-ran the audit's script from a copy in verify/rederive/ and all 32 checks pass. ENCODING. The audited result is an expectation by FO plus a search that found nothing. It is not a theorem, so no machine check can prove it. The script's sympy part checks the obstruction the later reviews name (T^split is not of positive type for NMC), not FO's sentence, and the audit says so openly; it does not offer the check as a proof that no absolute NMC QEI exists. I checked the kernel two independent ways. (i) I built the one-particle Gram matrix directly from the classical energy density |dtF|^2 + |gradF|^2 - 2xi Lap|F|^2 at momenta (1,0,0) and (0,2,0). It equals the script's K entry for entry (ratio 1), so the sign and normalisation are right. (ii) Averaging over the angle mu between k and k' reproduces the script's s-wave kernel Ks exactly. That makes the 2x2 minor a valid compression of the full kernel, so a negative minor does imply the full kernel is not of positive type. The quotes that carry the grade sit inside the pinned texts and are real string matches.

VACUITY. (a) Four mutated quotes are all absent: 'can also be derived', 'we have obtained an absolute QEI for the NMC field', 'removed for the non-minimally coupled field', and a version of the Kontou-Sanders sentence with its negation removed. Precision note, not a refutation: at xi<0 the kernel is also not of positive type numerically (minimum eigenvalue -0.53 at xi=-1/6), even though the s-wave 2x2 minor is +1/24 there. The audit's 'for every xi>0' is true, but the property actually tested is xi != 0, not the sign of xi.

verifiers.reason:
I checked the data row and the lacked_data answer at source. The grade STANDS. One detail in value_then is wrong, and the open contest resolves toward the tree.

(1) value_then misstates the history, though it does not change the conclusion. The audit says "the first curved-spacetime absolute QEI had just been proved, for the minimally coupled massive scalar only". Fewster-Smith's own text contradicts the "first curved-spacetime" part (gr-qc/0702056v3, cached, around line 308): "the only curved spacetime absolute QEI is that of Flanagan [25] ... massless free fields in two-dimensional globally hyperbolic spacetimes". Their abstract claims only "the first 'absolute' QEI ... on four dimensional globally hyperbolic spacetimes". 1809.05047v2 p.3 gives the same sequence: 2D flat [24], 2D curved [25], then 4D curved [26,27]. Kontou-Sanders call it "the first general absolute QEIs". The row should say "first absolute QEI in four-dimensional curved spacetime". The word "massive" is Fewster-Smith's abstract wording, but their body says mass mu >= 0. Neither correction changes "moves_conclusion: No".

(2) value_now is right. Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815v2 p.21 defines "absolute" as a lower bound Q(f) that is local and covariant, with an operator allowed. Their sentence "To date no absolute QEIs have been derived for the non-minimally coupled scalar field" (p.23, read in context) therefore covers state-dependent absolute bounds, as the audit reads it. The 2405.05963v2 and 2309.10848 quotes also check out in context.

(3) The open contest (1809.05047 p.3 citing math-ph/0611058) can now be adjudicated further. The alphaXiv quota had reset, and I read Sec. 3.2, Props 4.5 and 4.6, and App. B in full (pp.9-10, 13-14, 24-25):
- Prop 4.5 turns a STATE-INDEPENDENT locally covariant DQI into an AQI. FO's NMC DQI is state-dependent (Q = Q~ 1 + phi^2(S f), App. B), so Prop 4.5 does not apply.
- Prop 4.6 is about whether triviality carries over, not about getting an AQI from a DQI.
- The rearrangement route in Sec. 3.2 needs condition (10). The paper shows (10) only for the Wick square (App. A).
- App. B ends on p.25 with FO's difference QEI only, and claims no AQI for NMC.

So the 2018 sentence is not supported by the pages it cites. That is a discrepancy in a citing sentence. It is recorded, not repaired, and it refutes neither paper. Whether FO's DQI satisfies (10) is not checked in anything read here; that sub-point stays OPEN.

The audit's second grade-changer ("a reading of Props 4.5 and 4.6 showing they give such an AQI") has now been run and comes back empty.

(4) Literature search. discover_papers (keywords 'absolute quantum energy inequality' and 'non-minimally coupled scalar', recency first) returned only 0708.2450 and gr-qc/0606009. The NOT-FOUND persists. It is a search result over the alphaXiv index, dated 2026-10-02, and not a proof that no such bound exists.

(5) lacked_data answers M's hypothesis with evidence, not by assumption. No measured quantity enters an expectation. What FO lacked in 2007 was the outcome of the attempt, and the 2020-2024 reviews supply it: still not done, with the obstruction named (T^split is not of positive type). moves_conclusion follows.

Corrections the audit should carry: fix value_then to "first absolute QEI in 4D curved spacetime (Flanagan's 2D curved bound preceded it)". Change the math-ph/0611058 entry from "Sec. 3.2-5 NAMED-NOT-READ" to READ, recording that Prop 4.5 does not apply to a state-dependent DQI. Change the post-2024 search from NOT-READ to "run 2026-10-02, empty".

'q will be conjugate to p if and only if det A = 0 at q.' With G = sqrt(det A) (12): 'G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b] (13), where sigma_ab denotes the shear of the congruence of null geodesics emanating from p.' Kar & SenGupta eq (17): dTheta/dlambda + Theta^2/2 + sigma^2 - omega^2 = -R_ab k^a k^b, attributed to Sachs 1961. Olum 1998: 'The generic condition holds whenever there is any normal matter or any transverse tidal force anywhere on P ... From the generic condition, sigma cannot vanish everywhere, thus WEC implies theta < 0.' Gao & Wald p.9: under NEC + null generic condition + null geodesic completeness, 'every null geodesic in M contains a pair of conjugate points'.

rederivation.outcome: 24/24 PASS using sympy, z3 5.1.0 and numerics; output is in rederive/sachs-weyl-shear-focusing.out. S1: from A''=-TA with symmetric B=A'A^-1, sympy gives theta'=-theta^2/2-tr sigma^2-tr T and sigma'=-theta sigma-(traceless T) exactly; these are the Sachs optical equations. S2: the Jacobi formula and Gao-Wald eq 13 hold exactly, and the tree's u''=-qu is eq 13 with sigma dropped. S3: for exact Schwarzschild, R_kk=0 and the screen tidal matrix is T=diag(3ML^2/r^5, -3ML^2/r^5) with T12=0: traceless, linear in M, and the sign of M only swaps which eigendirection focuses. S4: z3 finds no traceless nonzero T without a focusing eigenvalue (unsat), and the vacuity guard is sat. S5: z3 is sat for q<=-|w|; numerically, q=-|w| kills the conjugate point and q=-|w|/2 delays it to 92.0. S6: Born integration reproduces the tree's 55.16 / 56.52 / 47.17 to within 1.3%. S7: the linearised metric's R_kk is zero at O(M), its O(M^2) residue defocuses, and composite's static check uses a non-null k. The first run failed S5c because the check itself was mis-specified (L=75 is shorter than the 91.4 focus); it was corrected and the correction is noted in the script.

audits.lacked_data: Nothing the conclusion uses is a datum. Sachs 1961 and Gao-Wald eq 13 are identities of the Jacobi equation, re-derived exactly here (S1, S2). That the Weyl term is traceless and sign-blind is exact algebra, checked on Schwarzschild for either sign of M (S3) and by z3 for any traceless symmetric 2x2 matrix (S4). No later measurement can move it, so M's hypothesis has nothing to act on for this result, and the evidence is that the statement holds symbolically with no numerical input. What 1961-2000 did not address is the NEC-violating regime: the theorems that turn shear focusing into conjugate points (Hawking-Ellis via Gao-Wald p.9, and Olum) assume NEC/WEC. That is a boundary of scope, not a gap in data, and computing across it (S5) shows the boundary matters: with q <= -|w| there is no conjugate point. Negative mass is prescribed in the tree, not observed, and the result holds for negative-mass Schwarzschild as a vacuum metric regardless.
audits.grade_evidence: Every use in vacuum STANDS. Eq 13 and the Sachs equations were re-derived exactly (S1-S2). The Schwarzschild tidal matrix is exactly traceless and sign-blind (S3-S4). The tree's vacuum conjugate points (56.50, 47.17) were reproduced independently to within 1.3% (S6). So the Lyapunov strike at seatindex.py:41-60 and 169-185 (lyapunov_excludes_weyl()=False) and lemma_is_shear_free_only at anecscope.py:59-72 and 206-211 are sound. The grade is NARROWED because two uses carry the statement past its hypothesis. seatindex.py:55-56 says Weyl focuses 'whatever q does', and anecscope.py:96-100 and 252-258 hard-code one_object_produces_both() as True. Both apply sign-blind Weyl focusing where T_kk<0, outside the NEC/WEC under which Olum 1998 and Gao-Wald p.9 derive conjugate points from shear. Computed here: if q<=-|w| there is no focusing eigenvalue (z3 sat), and at the tree's own parameters that removes the conjugate point (S5b). What narrows is a phrase and a constant, not a measurement; the per-ray conjugate points in anecscope were measured with the full matrix and stand. Two discrepancies are recorded and neither moves the conclusion: the linearised metric's R_kk is O(M^2), not exactly 0 (it defocuses, at 6.5e-4 of the Weyl power), and composite.py's static trace check uses a non-null k. The grade is not WRONG: nothing here contradicts the external result itself, only the widened reading.

verifiers.reason:
I could not refute NARROWED in either direction.

The audit could only re-derive the null shear equation (S1b) because alphaXiv was over quota. It answered this time, and I read the equation at source in a restatement: Perlick, 'Gravitational Lensing from a Spacetime Perspective', arXiv 1010.3416.
- p.14 eqs (16)-(18): the optical tidal matrix is Phi00*I plus a traceless Weyl block in Re/Im psi0. That confirms Weyl's contribution is traceless and sign-blind.
- p.16 eqs (25)-(26): sigma' = -sigma(rho+rhobar) + psi0, and 'the conformal curvature term psi0 directly produces shear'. This matches the audit's sigma' = -theta sigma - Psi0 up to sign and normalisation conventions.
- p.21 eq (44) and p.30: the focusing theorem and Hawking-Ellis Prop 4.4.5 are stated under 'the weak energy condition and the so-called generic condition'. This independently confirms the audit's point that turning shear focusing into conjugate points is a result proved under WEC/NEC.

I also checked the cached Gao-Wald text (gr-qc/0007021, eq 13 and the p.9 NEC+generic+completeness passage) and Olum (gr-qc/9805003: 'From the generic condition, sigma cannot vanish everywhere, thus WEC implies theta < 0'). Both are quoted accurately.

I re-ran the audit's script and got 24/24 PASS. I re-ran composite.survey read-only and got conjugate points 55.1667 / 56.5 / 47.1667 with traceless_ratio 0.00929 / 0.00839 / 0.01607, all as the audit reports. The cited lines check out: seatindex.py:55, anecscope.py:59, 69-70, 100, 182, 252, 300, 309, 350.

Why not STANDS: anecscope.py:96-100 and 252-258 hard-code one_object_produces_both() = True and say the seat and the escape 'cannot come apart' because Weyl is sign-blind. That conclusion needs Weyl focusing to beat Ricci defocusing along rays where T_kk < 0. Neither Sachs nor the read restatements supply that, since their conjugate-point results assume WEC/NEC, and the audit's S5 shows that with q <= -|w| there is no focusing eigenvalue. That is a real use outside the result's hypothesis.

Why not WRONG: nothing contradicts the external result itself.

Three caveats, none of which moves the grade:
1. The seatindex.py:55-56 'drift' is weak. The sentence is literally true of Weyl's contribution and sits inside a vacuum (q = 0) argument, so the narrowing rests on the anecscope sites alone.
2. The later_literature row marked effect 'contested' is mislabelled. That search was NOT-RUN, so 'contested' over-represents against the result; it should read NOT-RUN.
3. read_status can be raised. The null shear equation with its Weyl source is now READ in a restatement (Perlick 1010.3416 p.16). Sachs 1961 itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script myself, check whether it encodes the theorem or a toy of it, and run vacuity guards with the hypotheses negated
verifiers.reason:
The re-derivation reproduces. I copied the script to verify/rederive/swsf.py and it gave 24/24 PASS, exit 0, in 16 s, with the same values the audit reports: S1 and S2 have zero residual; Schwarzschild gives R_kk=0 and T=diag(+-3ML^2/r^5); z3 returns unsat for S4 and sat for its guard; Born integration gives 55.866, 55.866 and 46.693; S5b finds no conjugate point and S5c finds one at 92.009; S7 gives an O(M^2) R_kk of 2M^2(5x^2-2y^2-2z^2)/r^6, an integrated ratio of -6.55e-4, a null-k trace ratio of 8.77e-3 and a non-null-k ratio of 5.90e-5. A read-only run of composite.survey (python3 -B, git status clean) returns conjugate points 55.167, 56.5 and 47.167 and traceless_ratio values 0.00929, 0.00839 and 0.01607, which matches the audit.

Encoding. S1 and S2 are the real identities, not toys. They are symbolic over an arbitrary symmetric B and T, B' = -T - B^2 is the correct Riccati form, and the traceless part of B^2 is theta*sigma in 2D. The weak spot is S3. The general statement the tree relies on is that the screen trace of the optical tidal matrix is R_kk and its traceless part is the Weyl projection C_AkBk. S3 checks this only in vacuum, where it holds trivially. I closed that gap myself (rn2.py, curvature computed from exact symbolic metric derivatives and evaluated at 40 digits). The identity holds to better than 1e-41 on Reissner-Nordstrom with R_kk = 1.1e-3 (non-vacuum), on a Schwarzschild control, and on a generic metric with no symmetry and R_kk = 4.5e-2. The guard bites: with a non-null k the trace misses R_kk by 2.5e-2. So the sign-blind, traceless Weyl term does not depend on q in general, not just in vacuum.

Vacuity guards I ran (vguard.py; 9 of 10 RN-section lines were broken by a sympy 0*zoo nan at theta=pi/2 and superseded by rn2.py):
- With twist present (non-symmetric B), the theta identity fails with residual (b-c)^2/2. Adding +omega^2 restores it, which is the Kar-SenGupta eq 17 form.
- Eq 13 fails with a wrong coefficient of 1/3 or 1.
- S4 without the 'nonzero' clause is sat only at T=0.
- z3 confirms the eigenvalues of a traceless T are exactly +-sqrt(x11^2+x12^2).

Independent of Born, I integrated the Jacobi equation with RK4 along the exact bent Schwarzschild null geodesic. It gives 55.23 for M=+2e-3, 56.52 for -2e-3 and 47.15 for -4e-3, within 0.1% of the tree. This supports the audit's claim that the 1.2% Born offset is O(M^2) bending and that +M focuses earlier.

The script and audit overstate their rigour in places, but none of this changes the grade:
(a) Two of the 24 PASSes are hard-coded True and check nothing: S2c and S6r.
(b) S6s, equal conjugate points for +M and -M, holds by construction of the diagonal Born integrator, because swapping eigenvalues swaps u1 and u2. It is a tautology at O(M), not an independent test.
(c) S5a's z3 query is trivially sat.
(d) The profile q=-|w| in S5b and S5c is a constructed Ricci profile, not the tree's actual negative-core T_kk. It shows the mechanism alone does not guarantee a conjugate point. It does not show that any anecscope ray loses one.
(e) Misattribution: the audit says composite's static check 'reads 5.9e-5'. composite.tidal actually reads 1.62e-4 by finite differences. 5.9e-5 is the script's analytic value for the same non-null k. Both are far below the null-k 8.8e-3, so the conclusion does not move.

The tree sites are quoted accurately: seatindex.py:50-56 and 172-185, anecscope.py:59-70, 96-100 and 252-258 (one_object_produces_both returns True), and composite.py:28 and 43-44. The audit's reading of those sites holds:
- Every vacuum use STANDS.
- The phrase 'whatever q does' and the hard-coded True carry Weyl focusing into T_kk<0 territory, outside the NEC/WEC hypothesis under which shear yields conjugate points.
- The per-ray full-matrix measurements are untouched.

NARROWED is supported, not over-claimed either way.

audits.name: KF claim: rho < 0 (cos 2theta > sqrt2 eps) implies Delta > 1

source.located: C.-I. Kuo & L. H. Ford, 'Semiclassical gravity theory and quantum fluctuations', arXiv gr-qc/9304008 v1 (6 Apr 1993; TUTP-93-1, Feb 1993). Page 5 has (3.1)-(3.2). Page 6 has (3.7), (3.8) and the sentence after (3.8). Page 9 has the squeezed-state conclusion. The journal version, Phys. Rev. D 47, 4510 (1993), is NAMED-NOT-READ.

audits.published_statement: From v1 page 6, verbatim from the text layer: '... = K_ab K_mn 12 eps^2/(1+eps^2)^2. (3.7) From this result, Eq. (2.16), and the fact that K_00 = omega/(2L^3), we find that Delta(x) = (10 eps + sqrt2 cos(2 theta))/(12 eps). (3.8) From Eq.(2.16), it follows that the condition for the expectation value of energy density to be negative is cos(2 theta) > sqrt2 eps. In this case we have Delta(x) > 1. This indicates when the energy density is negative, the energy density fluctuations are large and the semiclassical theory is not a good approximation.' It uses (3.2) from page 5: 'Delta(x) = | (<:T00^2(x):> - <:T00(x):>^2) / <:T00^2(x):> | ... Note that we have used normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state to define the various operators.'
published_hypotheses: H1: a massless free scalar field in FLAT (Minkowski) spacetime, with the stress tensor bilinear (2.11) and minimal coupling.
H2: a single box-normalised plane-wave mode k in volume L^3, with K_00 = omega/(2L^3).
H3: the state (2.15), |Psi> = (|0> + eps|2>)/sqrt(1+eps^2), with eps REAL 'for simplicity' (page 4).
H4: T00 and T00^2 are both normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum (page 5).
H5: the coincidence limit of the purely temporal component, i.e. Delta(x) of (3.2), WITH the absolute value.
H6: the inference is drawn from KF's own (3.8), and from (2.16) for the sign condition. 'In this case we have Delta(x) > 1' is a corollary of (3.8), not an independent computation.
hypothesis_drift: SCOPE (named, not a drift against KF). The tree tests the claim against the EXACT Delta (fluctuation.py:55-58, 230, 237), not against KF's (3.8). As an inference FROM (3.8), KF's sentence is valid for every real eps != 0, with or without the absolute value (re-derivation C8, z3). The fault is upstream in (3.8), and the tree records that separately (KF_38_IS_EXACT = False, fluctuation.py:142). The tree's wording 'With the exact Delta that is FALSE' carries this scope correctly.

UNDERSTATED (in KF's favour, not M's). fluctuation.py:57 says 'z3 finds the counterexample', and data_used names a single witness (eps = 1/10, theta = 0). The truth is stronger. With the exact Delta, NO point of the family has both rho < 0 and Delta > 1 (C5: z3 returns UNSAT, and the vacuity guard is SAT). Exact Delta <= 1 on the whole (eps, theta) plane, with equality only at (sqrt2, cos2th = -1) and (-sqrt2, +1), where rho > 0 in both cases (C4). The claim fails at every rho < 0 point, not only at one witness.

DROPPED (harmless): the absolute value of (3.2). The tree writes the exact Delta as 1 - (2eps - sqrt2 cos2th)^2/(3(1+eps^2)), without the absolute value (fluctuation.py:40, 230, 237). On rho < 0 the bracket lies in (1/3, 1), so the absolute value changes nothing for this claim. On rho > 0 the bracket can reach -1 (the C4 equality points), where KF's Delta is +1. The tree's z3 test X^2 > 6(1+eps^2) (fluctuation.py:311) is the correct form of 'Delta > 1' once the absolute value is kept.

INHERITED (a KF-side discrepancy, harmless for the tree). KF's printed sign condition cos(2theta) > sqrt2 eps is exact only for eps > 0. With eps real, as KF state in H3, the condition reverses to cos2th < sqrt2 eps when eps < 0 (C10, z3, and a counter-point exists). The canonical name 'rho < 0 (cos 2theta > sqrt2 eps)' inherits the eps > 0 assumption, and the tree's sympy code declares eps positive (fluctuation.py:175). The tree's z3 hypothesis, however, is the sign-general e(2e - sqrt2 c) < 0 (fluctuation.py:305), so its refutation and T2 hold for every real eps. Replacing eps by -eps is equivalent to shifting theta by pi/2, so nothing physical moves.

DROPPED from the canonical list only: H1, H2, H4 and H5 (flat space, massless field, single box mode, Minkowski normal ordering, coincidence limit, 00 component). The canonical hypotheses list only 'vacuum + two-particle state', but the owner file states these (fluctuation.py:14-18) and its :T00: carries them (fluctuation.py:179-180). K_00 cancels in Delta, so the claim's truth value does not depend on the normalisation in H2 (C2-C3).

SCOPE (kept, correct). The tree limits the refutation to arXiv v1, marks PRD 47, 4510 NAMED-NOT-READ, and records that the page image was not viewed (fluctuation.py:122-126, 135-136). This audit keeps the same scope.

UNSTATED (named here). The reading of the sentence rests on the v1 text layer. It is corroborated internally: (3.8) as extracted gives Delta > 1 exactly when rho < 0 (C8), and the next sentence ('the energy density fluctuations are large') needs '>'. A mis-extracted inequality sign is therefore implausible, but the page image was not viewed.

audits.name: A pressureless (dust) thin shell with flat interior and Schwarzschild exterior is radially unstable (used as the validation fixture)

source.located: The tree names no source: stability.py:48 says 'as a dust shell must be' and stability.py:246 says 'as it must be'. The published result it relies on is the radial stability of a static thin shell with a Minkowski interior and a Schwarzschild exterior. That is Brady, Louko & Poisson, PRD 44, 1891 (1991), which is pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ. I read it through its exact reproduction in Ishak & Lake, arXiv:gr-qc/0108058v2, using eq (5) (Lake's potential), eq (7) (transparency), eqs (15)-(19) (the V''>0 criterion), sec. III.B and Fig. 2 ('R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0' at P'/sigma' = 1). The V''>0 criterion and the definition beta^2 = dp/dsigma come from Poisson & Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/9506083v1, eqs (13), (23) and (28). The adiabatic-index form comes from LeMaitre & Poisson, Am. J. Phys. 87, 961 (2019), NAMED-NOT-READ, via its restatement in Pitre-Schneider-Poisson arXiv:2604.05980v1 sec. X ('radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2'). The equation of motion for a genuine dust shell comes from Barcelo & Jaramillo arXiv:1112.5265v1, eqs (2)-(4).
source.via: alphaXiv page text. The alphaXiv quota ran out during this stage: answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers all returned 'quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses arxiv.org directly with a 403. I therefore read the verbatim alphaXiv page text that earlier calls in this same workflow had returned and cached under scratchpad d67/src/casmag/all/: gr-qc_0108058v2.txt (md5 26cf595d...), gr-qc_9506083v1.txt (1e67535c...), 1112.5265v1.txt (af75e731...) and 2604.05980v1.txt (9916ebc7...). BLP 1991 and LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 are known only through restatements. No source read states the fixture's exact claim (V''<0 at beta^2 = 0) word for word; I computed it in closed form from the formalism the sources give.

audits.published_statement: No source read states the result in the tree's words. What the sources do state: (i) Ishak-Lake eq (5): 'Rdot^2 = eps + ([m]/M)^2 - 2 eps mbar/R + (M/2R)^2 ... applies to both shells and wormholes', with stability meaning V''>0 (15). Sec. III.B gives Brady-Louko-Poisson's shell around a black hole: 'R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0 and R/m+ ~ 3 as m- -> m+' at P'/sigma' = 1. (ii) Poisson-Visser after eq (28): 'for V''(a0) > 0 ... stable, while for V''(a0) < 0 perturbations can grow (at least until the nonlinear regime is reached)'. (iii) PSP sec. X, restating LeMaitre-Poisson: such shells are 'radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2' (Newtonian). (iv) Barcelo-Jaramillo eq (4): a dust shell (p = 0) with a Minkowski interior obeys M = sqrt(1+adot^2) M0 - M0^2/(2a), with M0 constant. COMPUTED HERE: V''(R0) = [2 beta^2 (3s+1)s^2 + (s-1)(3s^2+2s+1)/2]/(s^2 R0^2), where s = sqrt(1-2M/R0). At beta^2 = 0 this is -(1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(2 s^2 R0^2) < 0 for every 0 < M/R0 < 1/2. Equivalently, Gamma_crit = (3s^2+2s+1)/(4s^2) >= 3/2.
published_hypotheses: A thin shell (Israel/Lanczos surface layer): timelike and spherically symmetric.
Vacuum on both sides: Minkowski inside (m- = 0), Schwarzschild outside with m+ = M > 0.
Transparency, with static embeddings near the shell (Ishak-Lake eqs 6 and 12, and dc/dr = 0).
Static equilibrium at R0 > 2M with V = V' = 0. This needs the Lanczos surface pressure p0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R0 s) > 0.
Linearised perturbations with l = 0 only. V''<0 means perturbations grow only 'until the nonlinear regime' (PV).
Barotropic matter described by beta^2 = P'/sigma', with PV's caveat that there is 'no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound' (sec. IV).
Gamma form: Gamma = d ln p / d ln sigma at fixed entropy (PSP eq 10.17). LeMaitre-Poisson use a different density convention.
Genuine dust (BJ): p == 0 exactly, so M0 = 4 pi a^2 rho stays constant.
hypothesis_drift: The label 'dust' for beta^2 = 0 (stability.py:48, stability.py:246, and stability.py:65 for the device). The code (stability.py:167-176, p = p0 + beta2 (sigma - sigma0)) computes a static shell whose Lanczos pressure p0 > 0 is held constant. That shell has zero pressure response, but it is not pressureless. A genuine dust shell has no static configuration at all: V = V' = 0 cannot be satisfied (checked with sympy and z3), and BJ eq (4) gives a_ddot = -(2Ma + M0^2)/(4a^3) < 0 at every instant. stability.py:45 ('no pressure response') and stability.py:241 ('at beta^2 = 0') state the hypothesis correctly. This is a discrepancy of wording, not of content. The canonical entry's name, 'pressureless (dust)', carries the same misnomer.
No source is given (stability.py:48, 246): the expected sign is simply asserted. It is now tied to BLP 1991 via Ishak-Lake, to LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 via PSP, and to the closed form computed here.

The tree tests three compactness values (M/R = 0.01, 0.1, 0.2 at stability.py:47-49 and 246-247). z3 proves the result for all 0 < M/R < 1/2. This strengthens the claim rather than cutting against the tree.

What the fixture does not check (stability.py:44 against stability.py:62-65). The fixture pins only the sign of V'' at beta^2 = 0. The device verdict also depends on the sign of the beta^2 coefficient, which the fixture never exercises. This audit closes that gap: the coefficient 2(3s+1)s^2 is positive (z3), and the tree's beta2_crit(ordinary) reproduces the exact values +0.003823 / +0.046477 / +0.122892 and Ishak-Lake's 2.37.

Hypotheses not restated at the validation (stability.py:39-50): vacuum on both sides, transparency, linearity, and beta not being a sound speed. They are carried by the Poisson-Visser machinery named at stability.py:39-42, and none of them changes the fixture's conclusion.

audits.lacked_data: The result is a closed-form theorem of classical general relativity. It uses no measured constant, observation or extrapolated datum, so no later data could move it. The sign of V''(beta^2 = 0) = -(1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(2s^2R^2) depends only on 0 < s < 1, and z3 proves it at every compactness. The evidence runs against M's hypothesis for this result: an independent closed-form re-derivation matches the tree's numbers, the published 2.37 (BLP via Ishak-Lake) and the Newtonian Gamma = 3/2 (LeMaitre-Poisson via PSP). What could change the physics is the model's assumptions, not data, and each is named: the thin-shell idealisation, beta treated as a sound speed (PV sec. IV), linearity, and l = 0 only. On the last, PSP 2026 found more instability (all l >= 2), not less. The one inaccuracy found is the tree's own word 'dust' for beta^2 = 0, which is a labelling discrepancy, not a flaw in the outside result.
audits.grade_evidence: I took the hypotheses exactly as the code computes them (stability.py:44-50, 167-176, 241-247): Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild outside, a static shell with Lanczos pressure p0 > 0, beta^2 = 0, and linear l = 0 perturbations. Under these, V''(R0) = -(1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(2s^2R0^2) < 0, and z3 proves it for every 0 < M/R < 1/2, where the tree samples only three points. The tree's printed values and its numerics match the exact form. The same form reproduces BLP's published 2.37 and LeMaitre-Poisson's 3/2. No datum enters. So the fixture's job holds: it does tell the sign convention apart, because a flipped convention would print V'' > 0 here. Recorded, but not moving the grade: (a) 'dust' misnames the beta^2 = 0 static shell (stability.py:48, 246, 65). A genuine dust shell has no static configuration (shown), while this one carries p0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0. The code keeps the correct hypothesis, so this is a discrepancy of wording, not a narrowed class. (b) The tree names no source. (c) The fixture does not exercise the beta^2 coefficient that stability.py:62-65 also depends on; this audit closes that gap (the coefficient is positive by z3, and the tree's beta2_crit matches the exact values). The grade is not NARROWED because the result holds on a larger class than the tree uses and the code drops no hypothesis. STANDS covers linear radial instability only.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the fixture is quoted as a claim about a literally pressureless static shell. That object does not exist, so the claim would hold only on the beta^2 = 0, p0 > 0 class. The correct wording is 'the zero-sound-speed static shell, with its Lanczos pressure p0 > 0, is linearly radially unstable at every compactness'. WRONG only if V''(beta^2 = 0) >= 0 is computed for some 0 < M/R < 1/2 under these hypotheses, which z3 rules out. RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it under sympy 1.14.0 and z3 5.1.0. Exit code 0, and all 32 checks print [ok]. The source quotes check out against the cached text: gr-qc_0108058v2.txt (md5 26cf595d) contains 'R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0' and '~ 3 as m- -> m+' at lines 420-426 and 703-710. gr-qc_9506083v1.txt (md5 1e67535c) contains 'nonlinear regime is reached' at line 525 and the sound-speed caveat at lines 835-838. stability.py --selftest prints SELFTEST OK.

ENCODING: THE THEOREM, NOT A TOY. The script derives V''(R0) in closed form for every compactness. It does not sample. It uses Lake's potential, the conservation law m_s' = -8 pi R p and the equation of state p' = beta^2 sigma'. These match what stability.py:_ms_at/V_second implements numerically. The closed form agrees with the tree's numbers to a relative error of at most 6e-5, from M/R = 0.01 up to 0.45. z3 proves the sign over the whole range 0 < s < 1. The fixture's own claim is only 'V'' < 0 at three sampled compactnesses, at beta^2 = 0, under PV machinery', and the audit proves strictly more than that.

I checked it independently in my own script, verify/rederive/dust-shell-verifier.py:
- (A) A Newtonian force balance, m Rddot = -m^2/2R^2 + 8 pi R p, which does not use Lake's potential. It gives V'' = 8 beta^2/R^2 - 3m/R^3. That matches the audit's weak-field limit (-3M/R^3) and the s -> 1 limit of the beta^2 coefficient (8/R^2). It also gives Gamma_crit = 3/2 exactly, which reproduces LeMaitre-Poisson's threshold independently.
- (B) A second published number the audit did not test. The general-M_in machinery at beta^2 = 1 puts the boundary at R/m+ = 2.3704 when m- = 0, and at 2.8612, 2.9851 and 2.9985 when m-/m+ = 0.9, 0.99 and 0.999. That matches Ishak-Lake/BLP's 'R/m+ ~ 3 as m- -> m+'.
- (E) A dynamic integration. I integrated Rddot = -V'/2 at M/R = 0.1, beta^2 = 0, starting 1e-6 off equilibrium. The perturbation grows monotonically from 1.0e-6 to 1.371e-5 by t = 8. That equals cosh(sqrt(-V''/2) t) to within 1%, so the shell genuinely runs away rather than oscillating.

VACUITY. The audit's own vacuity guard is weak. It only checks that 0 < s < 1 is satisfiable, which shows the hypotheses are consistent, not that the claim fails when they are negated. So I ran negation guards myself, and every one behaves correctly:
- With M > 0 negated (s > 1), z3 finds V''(beta^2 = 0) >= 0 reachable, at S = 2.
- With beta^2 = 0 negated, z3 finds V'' >= 0 reachable inside 0 < s < 1 (B = 2, S = 1/2).
- The same machinery applied to the device configuration (M_in = -0.01, M_out = 0) gives +2.9656e-2. That matches the tree's +2.965e-2, so the sign is not hard-wired into the machinery.
- The ordinary shell at M/R = 0.01 with beta^2 = 1 gives V'' = +7.91, which is stable.
- Mutating either sign convention (the conservation sign, or the sign of the Lanczos pressure) breaks the static condition V' = 0 (V' = +2.0e-2), so a convention error would have been caught.
The check therefore discriminates, and the claim is not vacuous.

1. The last check in section 8 is chk(..., True). It is declared, not computed, yet it is counted among the '32 checks'. Its content is trivially true, since beta^2 = 0 gives Gamma = 0.

The tree actually returns +0.003823, +0.046483 and +0.122935: bisection over a finite-difference V'' is off from the exact values by up to 4.3e-5. The rederivation outcome's word 'agrees' is accurate. The phrase 'exact values' overstates it.
3. The 'dust' misnomer is correctly recorded. The static beta^2 = 0 shell carries p0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0, and a genuine p = 0 shell has no static solution. The script shows both, with sympy and z3. NARROWED would apply only if the fixture were quoted as a statement about a literally pressureless static shell.

All four data rows hold, and the lacked_data answer rests on evidence rather than presumption. I found two small discrepancies. Neither moves any conclusion or the grade.

I wrote my own sympy derivation, independent of the audit's script, at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/data/dust_data_check.py. It uses the PV potential, m_s' = -8 pi R p, p = p0 + beta2 (sigma - sigma0), and a Minkowski interior, and solves V' = 0 for p0. It gives p0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R0 s), V(R0) = 0, and a V'' identical to the audit's closed form.

Row 1 (V'' at beta^2 = 0): the exact values are -3.0356e-2, -3.4238e-1 and -8.1694e-1. The tree prints -3.036e-2, -3.424e-1 and -8.169e-1 (stability.py:47-49), and those are the correct roundings. Calling stability.V_second directly gives -0.0303579, -0.342378 and -0.816937. The worst relative error is 6.0e-5, as the audit says.

Row 2 (BLP via Ishak-Lake): I read the cached gr-qc_0108058v2.txt (md5 26cf595d..., lines 420 and 703). Sec. III.B and the Fig. 2 caption both say "R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0" at P'/sigma' = 1. Solving V''(beta^2 = 1) = 0 gives R/M = 2.370393.

Row 3 (Gamma_crit): PSP 2604.05980v1.txt line 963 does read "radially stable whenever Gamma >= 3/2", with Gamma := (d ln p / d ln sigma)_s (eq 10.17). The audit's hypotheses cite that convention, but its value_now (3s^2+2s+1)/(4s^2) was computed with Gamma = beta2 (sigma+p)/p (rederive script, line 163). That is the relativistic-enthalpy convention, and the row does not state it. Under PSP 10.17 as cited, the threshold is Gamma_crit = beta2_crit sigma0/p0 = (3s^2+2s+1)/(s(3s+1)). At M/R = 0.2 that is 1.689, against the audit's 1.812. Both forms tend to 3/2 as M/R -> 0, and both exceed 3/2 for 0 < s < 1. For my form the condition reduces to (3s+2)(s-1) < 0. beta^2 = 0 gives Gamma = 0 in either convention, so moves_conclusion = No still follows. This is a discrepancy in the convention label, not a refutation of the row.

Row 4 (no physical datum): correct. V'' depends only on s and R0.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not presumed. The result is a closed-form statement whose sign holds for every 0 < s < 1. The audit's z3 check passes on rerun, and the factor (s-1)(3s^2+2s+1) shows it directly. It reproduces the published 2.37 and the 3/2 limit, so no missing datum could move it.

Two further observations, outside the data rows:
- The audit says the tree's beta2_crit(ordinary) "reproduces the exact values +0.003823 / +0.046477 / +0.122892". The tree actually returns 0.0038231, 0.0464834 and 0.1229345. That is agreement to a relative 1.3e-4 and 3.5e-4, from finite differences and bisection, not exact reproduction. This is a slight over-representation.
- BJ eq (4) reads M = sqrt(1+adot^2) M0 - M0^2/(2a), with p set to zero (1112.5265v1.txt lines 72-130). That supports the audit's point that a genuine dust shell has no static configuration.

audits.published_statement: The pass's tally, verbatim (journal): 'SIX FAMILIES RETURNED. THIS IS THE CONTROL (failure mode 1): the search apparatus returns positives, so the zero reported below is a measurement and not a dead search. ... solutions found with m(r) < 0 anywhere : 0; solutions found with negative ADM mass : 0; no-go theorem forbidding either found : 0. Status NOT-FOUND, not NOT-SEARCHED, and not NO.' The pass qualifies its own set. HPS is 'THE ONLY GENUINE NON-PERTURBATIVE SELF-CONSISTENT CONSTRUCTION IN THE SET'. APT is 'FIRST ORDER IN hbar ONLY ... not iterated to a fixed point'. Pinamonti et al. are 'not read at source'. The two estimate papers in their own words: KS (hep-th/0202068 p.10) write 'the self-consistent semiclassical wormhole, if exists, should possess the throat of sub-Planckian radius', and print eq. (62) 'E = -2c^4 a/G. Note that the total energy is negative.' They impose self-consistency only as 'the total energy must coincide with the ground state energy' (eq. 63), on an assumed flat-space thin-shell background r = |rho| + a (eq. 8). Garattini (gr-qc/0501105, titled 'Self sustained traversable wormholes?') assumes the Ellis background phi = 0, b = r_t^2/r (eqs. 14-16) and imposes only the integrated 'self-consistent equation for TT tensors' pi r_t/(2G) = -E_TT (eq. 41). How the tree uses it: throatmass.py:40-42 'No self-consistent semiclassical solution with m(r) < 0 or negative ADM mass, and no theorem forbidding one. NOT-FOUND, not NO.'; ledger.py:1729 and specthm.py:1084 '0 of 6 (self-consistent) families in print REPORT m < 0 -- true of what was reported'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (scope of the set): the six are what ONE search pass (DOCKET 62 O5) returned. They are not a census of what is in print.

H2 (reporting): 'm < 0 reported' is the pass's tally applied per family. It says what each paper REPORTS, not what the solutions' m(r) profiles are: HPS never print the flare profile, and APT's read pages print no mass-function sign.

H3 (self-consistency grade, per source): only HPS, Sanders and the Pinamonti line solve the semiclassical equations as a fixed point. KS and Garattini impose an INTEGRATED energy balance on an ASSUMED background (KS write 'if exists'; Garattini's title is a question). APT is a first-order linearised backreaction and is not iterated.
H4 (control scope, throatmass.py:57-60): the control shows the search returns SOLUTIONS. It is not shown able to surface a no-go theorem.
H5 (per-family sign basis, throatmass.py:137-159): throats are judged by m = r_0/2 at r' = 0 in the proper-distance gauge.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1 at ledger.py:1729 and specthm.py:1084. The wording '%d of %d (self-consistent) families IN PRINT REPORT m < 0' treats the pass's six as everything in print. throatmass.py:49-50 ('the same search returned self-consistent families') keeps H1. READ evidence that the six are not the whole literature: Arrechea-Breen-Ottewill-Pisani-Taylor arXiv:2607.07583v1 p.1 (banked text) cites horizonless configurations held up by vacuum polarisation that relax compactness bounds [18-20]: Arrechea-Barcelo 2305.07939; Arrechea-Barcelo-Carballo-Rubio-Garay PRD 109 104056 = 2310.12668; Reyes-Tomaselli 2301.00826. None is among the six. The superseded wording at ledger.py:1675-1678 ('%d self-consistent families are in print') has the same drift.

WEAKENED H3 at throatmass.py:122-126 and ledger.py:1729, where all six are counted as 'self-consistent families'. The journal's own qualifiers are not carried into the count: HPS is 'the only genuine non-perturbative self-consistent construction in the set', and APT is 'not iterated to a fixed point'. By the sources' own equations, three of the six are not fixed-point solutions of G = 8 pi <T>. KS and Garattini impose one integrated equality on an assumed metric (KS eq. 63, Garattini eq. 41), and APT is linear backreaction.

DISCREPANCY in H5 at throatmass.py:141-142 and at the selftest check throatmass.py:359-364. The KS row says 'throat (short-throat flat-space wormhole): m = r_0/2 > 0 at the throat', and the selftest applies m_throat = r_0/2 at a = 0.0141 l_P. But KS's metric (eq. 8) is r = |rho| + a, flat on both sides, so m = (r/2)(1 - r'^2) = 0 wherever it is defined (computed, C2), and the ADM mass is 0. The throat is a distributional shell (R = -8 a^-1 delta(rho), eq. 10) where r' is undefined, not a smooth r' = 0 throat. KS also PRINT a NEGATIVE total energy, E = -2c^4 a/G (eq. 62, reproduced in C2). This does not move the tally, because E is a proper-volume integral and is neither the Misner-Sharp m(r) nor the ADM mass. The family's basis is still misstated, and for this family 'zero negative mass' does not mean 'positive energy'. Recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation.

WEAKENED H2 where it is presented as a control of the zero (throatmass.py:49-53, 'the zero is a measurement and not a dead search'). Computed here (C2, C4): in FIVE of the six families m >= 0 is fixed by the symmetry class, or by the background the authors ASSUMED, before any semiclassical dynamics enters. Flat FLRW has m = R^3 H^2/2 >= 0 for every state. ESU has m = (a/2) sin^3 chi >= 0. Garattini's Ellis background has m = r_t^2/(2r) > 0. KS has m = 0. APT is Schwarzschild with M >> m_P at leading order. Only HPS could have returned m < 0 dynamically, and HPS do not print m beyond the throat. The control therefore shows that the search returns solutions, not that it returns solutions from a class where m < 0 is possible. The zero carries information about ONE family only.

ADDED: none. The tree adds no hypothesis the sources lack. Its own later work already demotes the tally: hpscentre.py:273 and :288 set M_NEGATIVE_FOUND_IN_HPS_SYSTEM = True, first at 0.0516 l_P, in the CONSERVED reading only, and ledger.py:1729-1731 now calls the tally 'true of what was reported, and no longer the tree's finding'.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (22 checks). C1: the journal block lists exactly six numbered families and its tally lines read 0 / 0; throatmass.py's derived counts (6, 0, 3) match. C2 (sympy, Misner-Sharp mass from each metric): flat FLRW gives m = R^3 H^2/2 >= 0 identically. ESU gives m = (a_0/2) sin^3 chi >= 0. Garattini's Ellis background gives m = r_t^2/(2 sqrt(l^2+r_t^2)) > 0, going to 0 at infinity (ADM mass 0). KS's r = |rho| + a gives m = 0 off the shell (ADM mass 0). KS eq. (62), E = -2a, is reproduced from eq. (61) with r'' = 2 delta(rho). The HPS throat has m(0) = r_0/2 and m''(0) = aa(1-2 r_0 aa)/2, which is 0 at r''(0) = 0. An illustrative check (not HPS data): the flare form HPS print, R ~ l plus a bounded wiggle, has m < 0 wherever the wiggle's slope is positive. C3 (banked source text): KS print 'Note that the total energy is negative.' and 'if exists'. a = l_P sqrt(f/2) with f ~ 4e-4 gives 0.01414 l_P (printed 0.0141), and 0.16/0.0141 = 11.35 m_P (printed 11.35). Garattini's (78) x (79) arithmetic, 1.158822606 x 0.3860531213 = 0.44736708408, matches the printed 0.4473670842. C4: m >= 0 is forced by class or assumed background in 5 of the 6 families, and the tree's own hpscentre flag M_NEGATIVE_FOUND_IN_HPS_SYSTEM is True. throatmass.py --selftest was also re-run: SELFTEST OK.

audits.lacked_data: What the pass lacked, and whether it moves the tally. (1) THE FLARE PROFILE OF HPS. HPS never print m(l) beyond the throat: p.8 gives only R ~ l with 'Planck-scale wiggles' and F ~ (a ln l - b)^2. So the pass could only record 'not reported'. The tree later computed the profile and found m < 0 in HPS's own conserved system at 0.0516 l_P (hpscentre.py). The 1997 authors did not publish this and the pass did not have it. It does not change what HPS REPORT, but in the conserved reading it changes 'zero in the returned families' from 0 to 1, and that finding lies outside the AHS established domain. (2) THE BOULWARE-STATE SELF-CONSISTENT LITERATURE (Arrechea-Barcelo-Carballo-Rubio-Garay 2020-2024 and successors). It is absent from the six; the READ evidence of the gap is 2607.07583v1 p.1. If that is confirmed at source, the literature-level statement 'no self-consistent semiclassical solution with m(r) < 0' is false for SINGULAR, non-regular-centre, regularised-Polyakov solutions. That is the same exclusion the tree's RN control already names (D4, regular centre). The tally would then survive only as 'what one pass returned'. Against reading this in M's favour: none of it is READ, none of it is regular-centre or rests on a rigorously established RSET, and none of it has been shown to be asymptotically flat with m < 0 and a regular centre. (b) SELF-CONSISTENCY: by the sources' own equations, KS (eq. 63, 'if exists') and Garattini (eq. 41, title ending in '?') impose one integrated energy balance on an assumed background, and APT is first-order linear backreaction. 'Six self-consistent families' therefore holds for three: HPS, Sanders and the Pinamonti line. (c) CONTROL STRENGTH: computed with sympy, m >= 0 is fixed by the symmetry class or the assumed background in 5 of the 6 families (flat FLRW m = R^3 H^2/2; ESU m = (a/2) sin^3 chi; Ellis m = r_t^2/2r; KS m = 0; APT Schwarzschild at leading order). verifiers.reason:
NARROWED survives. alphaXiv answered this stage, so I read the two papers the audit carried as NAMED-NOT-READ at source.

(1) arXiv:1911.03213v2 (Arrechea, Barcelo, Carballo-Rubio and Garay, PRD 101 064059). On pp.1 and 5 the paper finds all self-consistent static vacuum solutions of G = 8 pi hbar <T>, using a Regularized Polyakov RSET in the Boulware state. On p.10 it says: 'm(r) grows from its asymptotic value M up to a value at the throat given by r_B/2. Then, it starts decreasing reaching -infinity at the internal asymptotic region.' The exterior is asymptotically flat with M > 0, and the interior is a null naked singularity at finite proper distance. pp.10-12 also give a self-consistent negative-ADM-mass branch with a naked singularity at r = 0, and p.10 adds 'none which is regular, with the exception of the Minkowskian solution.'

(2) arXiv:2105.11261v2, p.7: super-critical stars have 'negative divergent compactness and Misner-Sharp mass at r = 0'. On p.17, m grows inward from M_ADM in the vacuum region, so m > 0 there.

A self-consistent semiclassical solution with m(r) < 0 is therefore in print, now READ. ledger.py:1733 asks O5 as 'exist at all?', so the tree's zero does not hold as a statement about the literature. It holds only as a record of the pass and under hypotheses the tree has not fully named. The audit's own conditional covers this case: 'beyond a singular neck -> NARROWED stands'. It does not reach WRONG, because throatmass.py:40-42 is worded NOT-FOUND, which is accurate of the pass, and no regular or exact-RSET counterexample is READ. The audit's 'Not WRONG: no READ counterexample' must now read 'no READ regular, exact-RSET counterexample'.

One correction to the audit. For 1911.03213 the negative-m region has no centre, since r goes to +infinity inside the neck. So the hypothesis to name is not the regular centre (D4). It is NON-SINGULAR (no curvature singularity at finite proper distance on either side of a neck), together with an exact or rigorously established RSET; the paper uses an s-wave Polyakov approximation with regulator alpha > 1. published_hypotheses: The shell is infinitesimally thin and traces a timelike hypersurface. The unperturbed state is static and spherically symmetric (p.2, p.7).
Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild outside, vacuum on both sides (p.7).
The shell matter is a perfect fluid with isotropic surface pressure, Eq (2.2).
The equations of state are barotropic, mu = sigma + eps(sigma) and p = p(sigma), Eq (2.4). Here sigma is the areal rest-mass density and mu the areal energy density.
The fluid is isentropic and obeys the first law dmu = (mu+p)/sigma dsigma, Eq (2.5). Eq (2.7) rests on this.
Gamma := d ln p/d ln sigma, taken in the rest-mass density, Eq (2.6). In general it depends on sigma.
Israel junction conditions, Eq (2.10), in general relativity.

The criterion is a turning-point criterion: dM/dsigma >= 0 along the equilibrium sequence. The paper does not derive that this point is where dynamical radial instability begins; it cites Ref [34] for that. It also assumes the sequence starts stable at low sigma (p.9).

Page 8 gives the Minkowski/Schwarzschild junction, Eqs (3.3)-(3.10). From those, (3.11)-(3.12) follow, and they match wall.statics: wall's variable named 'sigma' is the energy density mu, not the rest-mass density.

Independent sympy re-derivation (verify/refute/gamma1_refute.py, exit 0). It does not use the auditor's script.
- It uses the shell equation of motion V = 1-(M/m+m/(2R))^2 with m = 4 pi R^2 mu, mu' = -2(mu+p)/R and p' = beta^2 mu'.
- It gives V = V' = 0 at equilibrium and a single V'' root, beta^2_crit = (1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(4s^2(3s+1)). This equals wall.beta2_crit, and dV''/dbeta^2 = 2(3s+1)/R^2 > 0, so stability needs beta^2 > beta^2_crit, the same direction wall uses.
- Converting by (2.7) gives Gamma - Gamma_1(3.16c) = 0 identically.
- (3.16a) equals (3.16c).
- The turning point of M(mu,p) from (3.13), with the first law, has the single root Gamma = 3/2+4q+4q^2.
- beta^2_crit = 1 gives R/M = 2.370393.
- wall.py --selftest exits 0.

So the content of the tree's use holds: same configuration, same Gamma definition, an exact identity, no empirical datum, and the source's own hypotheses. The hypothesis drift does not undermine STANDS. The source attributes dynamical onset to the turning point and cites [34] for it; that pointwise reading is closed by the independent V'' route. The dropped barotropic/isentropic/first-law hypothesis is satisfied by the tree's radial matter models. I found no misreading that would push the grade toward NARROWED or WRONG. The attribution to LeMaitre-Poisson is a discrepancy in form, which the auditor recorded correctly as not a content error.

One small imprecision in the audit, which does not move the grade. The audit says wall.gamma_crit's double-precision error is 'up to 9.8e-11 on [1e-6, 0.8]'. That is the maximum relative error on the auditor's 806-point grid, not the true maximum. Finer sampling near x = 1e-6 gives absolute residuals up to 2.5e-10, about 1.7e-10 relative. II p.3: the compactified case is 'very much analogous to the Casimir effect. ANEC is violated on any geodesic that does not remain at constant z. However, no such geodesic is achronal.' In Schwarzschild (Boulware vacuum), 'every complete geodesic ... is chronal.' Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007, abstract: 'the ANEC holds in flat space with boundaries, as in the Casimir effect, for geodesics which stay a finite distance away from the boundary.' p.2: the plate system is not expected to violate ANEC 'because geodesics parallel to the plates do not violate the NEC, while any other geodesic eventually intersects the plate material.' p.3: 'ANEC may be violated in general curved spacetimes', and it is violated in flat space with a periodic identification 'along any null geodesic which winds around the compact direction ... essentially the Casimir system without the plates.' The result rests on no measured datum: its inputs are computed QFT constants (pi^2/720, pi^2/90, the anomaly coefficient), and the conclusions the tree uses are signs, so no later measurement can move them. What the earliest work lacked was later calculation, and that moved in both directions. First, the plate system was shown to OBEY ANEC (Graham-Olum 2005; Fewster-Olum-Pfenning 2007). The tree has not taken this in, and the resulting mistake is the tree's, not the outside literature's. Second, violations on curved backgrounds were extended to ACHRONAL geodesics for test fields (Urban-Olum 2010), which strengthens the headline the tree quotes. Neither changes the tree's working conclusion that violating ANEC is not by itself a disqualification. What they change is which system is the counterexample, and why it escapes achronal ANEC.
audits.grade_evidence: The HEADLINE stands on sources READ: 'ANEC in curved spacetime is false in general, so violating it is not by itself a disqualification'. Those sources are G&O 0705.3193 (abstract and Sec. II, Schwarzschild/Boulware), FOP p.3, Visser gr-qc/9409043 p.1, and Urban-Olum 0910.5925 (achronal case; eq.42 evaluates to -2.116e-7). The tree says 'a geodesic between the plates violates it' and 'Casimir escapes because the geodesic between the plates is not achronal'. Against that, the sources say the plate system OBEYS ANEC (FOP abstract and p.2; G&O p.2; KS p.34). Computation here agrees: T_kk = 0 on every parallel geodesic (EM, and a scalar of any mass, any xi, Dirichlet or Neumann); every other geodesic hits a plate; and every null line between plates is achronal (z3). The Casimir-type counterexample that does exist is the plate-free compactified Minkowski space. Its violating geodesics wind and are chronal (covering interval -L^2), and it is flat, not curved. So the result holds for a smaller, different class than the tree states: the headline holds, and the example holds only as the compactified vacuum. The plate wording at anecscope.py:26, :33-34, :167 and obstruct.py:164-165 is a computed discrepancy, and it is recorded, not repaired. It is not graded WRONG overall because nothing resting on it moves. obstruct.py's ANEC row and index3 ANEC-RELOCATES use only 'violating ANEC is not a disqualification', and the curved counterexamples READ here carry that. The tree's escape mechanism (chronality, 'same as GJW', anecscope.py:109) is exactly the compactified-Casimir mechanism. It is not graded STANDS because the example as used is contradicted.

- B: the decomposition T_kk = <(k.dphi)^2> - xi (k.d)^2 <phi^2> is the correct algebra for a null k, at any xi. The image sum uses an arbitrary f(sigma), so it covers any mass and both Dirichlet and Neumann conditions.

TOY vs THEOREM. Parts A and B are a finite check on IDEAL plates only: EM between perfect conductors, and image-sum scalar boundary conditions. They are not FOP's theorem, which covers a tubular flat neighbourhood. Still, ideal plates are the system the tree names, and the check is enough to contradict 'a geodesic between the plates violates it'.
- One limit is unnamed in the script, though the audit names it under what_would_change: real dispersive plates. In that case T_ab(z) is not boost-invariant along the plates. Tracelessness plus x-y symmetry gives T_kk(parallel) = (3T_tt - T_zz)/2. That is zero for ideal plates, but it need not be zero when T_tt varies with z. So the computed T_kk = 0 is an ideal-plate result.
- Part D's z3 lemma (future timelike plus future causal is timelike) is the standard local step, not the full achronality theorem. The slab is convex, so it is enough.

- Timelike instead of null parallel k: the image term is nonzero, 2f'(4n^2a^2).
- k across the plates, with the full contraction including cross terms: nonzero for both translated and reflected images.

- z3 with time orientation dropped, with v spacelike, or with u null instead of timelike: each turns sat.
Every check therefore fails when its hypothesis is removed, so none of them is vacuous.

source.located: This is a composite, kind 'computation': the tree's own juxtaposition (tolman.py:1459-1527, V17 at tolman.py:1775-1778) of three external results. (1) T. H. Boyer, Phys. (2) The Deutsch-Candelas near-wall EM stress for a curved perfect conductor, A_EM = 1/(60 pi^2), via Milton arXiv:1005.0031 eq. (58); the interior form is Saharian arXiv:0708.1187 eq. 14.21. (3) Sopova & Ford arXiv:quant-ph/0504143 eq. (15), the planar plasma-model transverse coefficient K = sqrt2 omega_p/(128 pi), whose origin is quant-ph/0204125 eq. (37). The spherical plasma prefactor p_r = +K/(a eps^2) is the tree's RECONSTRUCTION (tolman.py:1057-1060, 1157).

audits.published_statement: Boyer, via Milton 1005.0031 eq. 117 and Table 1: the Casimir self-stress of a perfectly conducting spherical shell of negligible thickness is S_EM = +0.04618/a^2, repulsive. Milton eq. (58): near a sphere, for conformal fields, <T^{mu nu}> = (A/eps^3) diag(2/a, 0, a, a sin^2 theta), with A = 1/(60 pi^2) for EM with perfect-conductor boundary conditions; this is traceless and has no cubic divergence in T^rr. Sopova-Ford 0504143 eq. (15): 'T_xx ~ (1/2) U ~ (sqrt2 omega_p/(128 pi)) (1/z^3), as z -> 0' for a plasma half-space, with T_zz independent of z. Sopova-Ford 0204125 Sec. 3.4: 'the inclusion of dispersion ... reduces the power in z up to two orders'. Sec. 3.5: the perfect-conductor <E^2> ~ 3/(16 pi^2 z^4) comes back only in the limit eps -> infinity. The divergence is 'not considered to be physical' and is attributed to the sharp boundary. THE TREE'S COMPOSITE, which no external paper states: ledger.py:1547-1552 'The sign INVERTS for any real mirror at a_c = 0.480 x skin depth, materials-independent'; ledger.py:2130-2133 B3 'm(r) > 0 near the wall for every real mirror'; specthm.py:1244-1245 'S2 because the Casimir sign inverts for real mirrors'.
published_hypotheses: Boyer: a perfect conductor at all frequencies, an infinitesimally thin shell, interior and exterior summed so that the surface divergences cancel, T = 0, flat space. It is a TOTAL (global) quantity.

Deutsch-Candelas / Milton eq. (58): conformal field, ideal boundary condition, only the leading eps^-3 surface term, eps << a. It needs perfect reflection at the frequencies ~c/eps that dominate the near-wall sum, which for a plasma mirror means eps >> c/omega_p.

Sopova-Ford eq. (15): planar geometry, collisionless plasma model, SHARP step boundary (which the authors name as the cause of the divergence), omega_p z << 1, T = 0, a local, isotropic, non-magnetic medium.

Tree's reconstruction: the planar transverse term K/eps^3 carries over to the concave side of the sphere, and p_r = o(eps^-3). Conservation then fixes p_r = +K/(a eps^2) inside. Status RECONSTRUCTED, 'sign and order only' (tolman.py:1057-1060).
Tree's identity: m(r) c^2 = 4 pi r^3 p_r(r) for a traceless, conserved, static source with a regular centre, read as a test field, on a ball strictly inside the cavity.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: the two asymptotes hold in disjoint ranges of eps. tolman.py:1517-1527 and V17 (tolman.py:1775-1778) form (K/(a eps^2))/(A/(a^2 eps^2)) 'with eps CANCELLING EXACTLY', which treats the ideal term and the plasma term as coexisting at one eps. The ideal asymptote needs eps >> lambdabar_p; the plasma asymptote needs omega_p eps/c << 1. On the exact planar plasma integrals (C4): <E^2>/ideal is 0.00074 at omega_p z = 1e-3 and 0.9984 at 1e3; <E^2>/plasma is 0.99918 at 1e-3 and 0.00135 at 1e3. If the ideal term were additive, exact/plasma would be 1351.5 at 1e-3; the measured value is 0.99918, so near the wall the ideal term is replaced, not out-competed. At the point where the two asymptotes are equated (omega_p z* = 1.3505), the exact value is 0.4841 of either. For the sphere this is argued from the planar computation, not computed: when a <~ lambdabar_p the ideal asymptote has no domain at all, and a = a_c falls in that case. a_c is therefore not a physical threshold.

WIDENED 'near the wall' (ledger.py:2130-2133 B3; ledger.py:1547-1549). Under the reconstruction, p_r > 0 (so m > 0) only where eps <~ lambdabar_p (gold 21.93 nm), and this holds for every radius, not only for a > a_c. For a >> lambdabar_p, the band lambdabar_p << eps << a follows the ideal p_r = -hbar c/(60 pi^2 a^2 eps^2) < 0, so m < 0 there. This is argued, not computed, for a sphere.

STATUS FLATTENED: ledger.py:1547-1552 and specthm.py:1244-1245 leave out that the spherical plasma prefactor is RECONSTRUCTED (tolman.py:1057-1060, 1157) and drop every hypothesis. The sign of the reconstruction is supported by conservation (C1).

WIDENED 'materials-independent' (ledger.py:1549; tolman.py:1525, 3041, 3265 'FOR EVERY CONDUCTOR'). The SIGN of the near-wall material coefficient holds for every passive, local, sharp-boundary medium: eps(i zeta) > 1 puts the integrand in (0,1) (z3, C3d). The NUMBER 0.480 holds only for the plasma model: Drude damping moves it by -0.1747 %, and an illustrative interband term by +14.67 % (which would give a_c = 0.4187 lambdabar_p).
DROPPED: the sharp boundary and the atomic scale. No owner site names either, and together they bound the inversion zone from below.

UNNAMED SIDE: ledger.py:2130-2133 does not say 'interior'. Outside the sphere the plasma term gives p_r = -K/(a eps^2), the opposite sign (C1b). The tree's use is interior, so this is a scope to name, not an error.

LABEL DISCREPANCY (not a refutation): the S2 row is named 'Casimir between ideal plates' (ledger.py:1546), but its note argues a curvature inversion for real curved mirrors. A single flat plasma plate has no near-wall T_zz divergence to invert (0504143 eq. 13).

NAME vs CONTENT: 'Boyer' refers to a TOTAL, while the tree's claim is LOCAL. Whether the total changes sign for real shells is CONTESTED (Bordag-Khusnutdinov 0801.2062; Graham-Quandt-Weigel 1305.5144). No owner site claims that the total inverts.

It supports a real-mirror sign difference for the total and says nothing about the local p_r.

For a plasma delta-shell, Boyer's value is recovered for Omega R >> 1 and the stress is attractive for R <~ 1/Omega (E ~ -0.0589 sqrt(Omega R)). This disagrees with 1305.5144 at large R, because the model and renormalisation differ.
